applicant_utility.summary: Up to 76 awards of €8,000 gross a year plus a student-fee waiver for international students admitted to an English-taught Padua degree, paid in two €4,000 instalments. There is no scholarship form at all: your degree application is the application, so the deadline you must watch is the admission deadline of the programme you pick, and applying in the first admission call genuinely improves your odds because the awards are mainly reserved for those candidates. You will need to move your residence to Padua and hold an Italian or SEPA IBAN before any money reaches you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Italian, non-Italy-resident applicants with an outstanding academic record who apply in the first admission call for an English-taught Padua bachelor's, master's or single-cycle degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the English-taught programme listed in the call for applications, since only those programmes carry the scholarship
Apply in the first call for admission rather than waiting, because selection starts from first-call applicants and only spills over if places remain
Prepare to accept both the admission offer and the scholarship offer, since declining either loses the award
Plan the residence transfer to Padua and open a bank account or prepaid card with an IBAN in your own or joint name before payment is due
Set aside the regional fee and revenue stamp for each academic year, which remain payable
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the programme's admission deadline, since eligibility for the scholarship depends on eligibility for admission
Missing the first call for admission and losing the priority that first-call applicants receive
Losing fewer than 20 credits by 30 November of the following academic year, which revokes the award
Failing to accept both the admission offer and the scholarship offer
Transferring to another degree programme or university or withdrawing from study, which triggers repayment of the amount received
Moving residence to Padua only after the payment window, which delays or blocks the instalment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The regional fee and the revenue stamp for each academic year, living costs in Padua and travel from home.
document_audit: No separate scholarship application, documents or essay is required - the degree application is the whole file
Admission requires a non-Italian secondary diploma (bachelor's and single-cycle) or a non-Italian academic qualification (master's)
The award is granted for the duration of the programme, so renewal is automatic in principle but conditional on the credit rule
alerts: The awards are mainly reserved for first-call applicants, so a late second-call application can realistically miss out even if you are stronger on paper
Results are published on the University website rather than sent individually, so check the admissions results page rather than waiting for email
The 2027/28 call is expected in November 2026, with a first application window closing on 15 November 2026 - a genuinely tight turnaround
The credit rule is absolute: fewer than 20 CFU by 30 November revokes the scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the English-taught degree within its admission deadline, check the University's admissions results page for the Teaching Committee outcome, then accept both the admission and the scholarship, move residence to Padua and provide an IBAN to start receiving €4,000 instalments.

applicant_utility.summary: A €7,200 annual scholarship for non-EU citizens living abroad, rising to €8,500 for women on STEM programmes, awarded through the admission ranking of the relevant call rather than through any scholarship form, and paired with a tuition exemption for that year. The money is conditional from the start: the second instalment depends on earning at least half your first-year credits in the January and February exam sessions, or 42 credits by 10 August, and the University re-checks every September whether you keep the award. Because there is no separate application, applying to the right non-EU admission call is the entire game.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU citizens living abroad with a strong admission application to a Trento two-year or single-cycle degree programme, particularly women applying to STEM programmes where the award is larger.
application_readiness_checklist: Find the current call for non-EU citizens residing abroad and treat that call's deadline and document list as the scholarship deadline and document list
Confirm your target programme is a two-year or single-cycle degree and not a Master of Arts, which is excluded
If you hold an Italian qualification, check your eligibility before assuming the international route, since Italian qualification holders are directed to the Italian national scholarship
Plan your first-year exam schedule around the January and February sessions, since the second instalment depends on credits earned there
Understand that failing the credit test can leave you repaying part of the award and paying fees at the applicable rate
common_rejection_risks: Missing the non-EU citizen call deadline or submitting an incomplete application, which makes you ineligible entirely
Being placed outside the scholarship positions in the admission ranking
Failing to earn at least half of the first-year credits in the January and February sessions and not reaching 42 credits by 10 August
Losing credits by the 10 August check, so the September verification does not confirm you for the next academic year
Applying as an Erasmus Mobility or visiting student, or to a Master of Arts, all of which are excluded
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Trento or Rovereto beyond the scholarship, plus flights and any regional fees not swept into the tuition exemption.
document_audit: There is no scholarship file of its own, so every document you submit in the admission call serves double duty
The gender-based STEM uplift means two applicants with identical profiles can receive different amounts, so check your programme's STEM status rather than assuming the lower figure
alerts: The University states that it checks credits earned by 10 August and confirms or refuses the scholarship for the following academic year in September, so every autumn is a re-qualification
Male applicants in STEM programmes do not receive the €8,500 amount, and the remaining funds available to non-STEM female applicants shift proportionally as a result
The number of scholarships is described only as limited, so do not treat admission as a guarantee of funding
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply in the non-EU citizen admission call for your programme, watch the admission ranking, then honour the credit milestones: the first instalment by December of the first year, the second by May or, failing that, by October once the 42-credit fallback is met.
